name: Weight tracker
intro: Where the weight diary is honest and shame-free, and where history gets lost and subscription traps wait.

apps.title: Weight Diary
apps.verdict: A time-tested simple weight diary with badges and motivation, like levels in a game. You enter the day's weight, keep notes and watch the trend, and many use it for Mounjaro and Ozempic. Its weak spots are honest, the paid version only removes ads and does not migrate months of data automatically, and there is no backup import.
apps.loved: Simple and stable, people track weight here for years, and the badges and motivation genuinely keep you engaged. Handy for tracking Mounjaro weight loss, and there is a passcode lock.
apps.weak: The paid version only removes ads and does not carry over months of data, so you re-enter it. A full graph is hard to find, and the old passcode protection went missing in one version.
apps.whoFor: People who want a reliable simple weight diary for the long haul, including alongside GLP-1, and who value privacy and motivation.

quotes.text: I have to unlink my Fitbit account and then relink it in order for it to register my last weigh in. Please fix this.
when I enter my goal, when it's put in on settings it shows what I need to do to get there by that date, but when I go to home screen it just shows 1 pound a week.
Seems pretty simple, but the app really helps keep me motivated and focused. actually helps me decide not to have a late night snack. Works like badges you earn in video games!
I’ve been using this app to track my weight for more than 5 years. It has been helpful and indispensable.

apps.title: Weight Diary Lite
apps.verdict: A deliberately simple weight and BMI tracker with no calorie counter and no extra screens. You enter only the day's weight and can skip days. Importing historical data is not supported, and the built-in goal calculator used to lie and suggest eating 500 calories a day, which is dangerous misinformation.
apps.loved: Maximum simplicity, just weight and nothing extra, and you do not have to log every day. A passcode hides the number from prying eyes.
apps.weak: You cannot import old data even manually, and the graph shows only a couple of weeks. The goal calculator gave harmful 500-calorie advice, and the lock screen was removed in the new version.
apps.whoFor: People who just want to log weight and BMI without calories or settings, and who care about keeping the number private.

quotes.text: This "would" have been a good app if a goal calculator was included. A goal calculator is advertised on the screen shot, but no where to be found once downloaded.

apps.title: Shotsy GLP-1 Tracker
apps.loved: Easy shot and injection-site logging, motivating progress view, GLP-1 focus, reminders, useful free version for basics
apps.weak: More tools pushed behind the paywall, shots silently fail to log, total data loss when switching Android and iPhone, review prompt after every shot, crashes with a second medication
apps.whoFor: People on GLP-1 who want a focused injection and weight tracker and will likely pay for pro

quotes.text: everything worked fine until recently when I noticed it’s not logging my shots. I click add shot on shot day like usual and it appears to add it but then the next day when I open the app it says I never added my shot.
I can keep track of every part of my weight loss journey with my GLP-1 and I love the reminders and how they encourage you when you’ve lost weight.

apps.title: WeightDrop Weight Loss Tracker
apps.verdict: A long-running minimalist weight tracker with cheerful reward notes for pounds lost. You weigh in daily and scroll through history. After a major update the graph started showing only monthly averages, the entry step was coarsened to half a pound, and some people lost years of records moving to the new version.
apps.loved: Simple and uncluttered, with funny notes like losing five pounds is worth 175 silver coins. Scrolling history and daily weigh-ins over years work well.
apps.weak: The update coarsened the weight step to half a pound and cut the graph range to three months. Some people lost years of history, CSV export crashes the app, and there is no iCloud sync.
apps.whoFor: People who weigh in daily and love minimalism with a touch of humor, if they can live with a coarse weight step.

quotes.text: Big app mis-step in removing the ability to add full incremental weights. You were founded on accurate and concise data. That’s what everyone wants managing weight and tracking trends. Yes, we’re only talking tenths of a pound, but that matters.
when I set the daily weight it doesn’t show the whole weight for most of the numbers so I’m sort of guessing what number I’m choosing.
This version won't let you go back to any timeframe shorter than 3 months, so the graph compresses the data points all together. I want a cleaner view of my progress for just the past month.

apps.title: Monitor Your Weight
apps.loved: Clear trend graphs, easy weight entry, keeps long weight history, size measurements too, motivates coming back to goals
apps.weak: Wipes years of history at once, shaky sync with Apple Health, Withings and watch, explicit ads at top of screen, tiny text, crashes on tab switch
apps.whoFor: People who want a simple weight logger with strong trend graphs and can back up data elsewhere

quotes.text: I bought the paid version and it is not currently syncing with my Withings scale. It did at first, but is not now. It also is not keeping my preferred goal weight saved.

apps.title: ControlMyWeight
apps.loved: Clean tracking with no bloat or ads, no forced signup, strong food and calorie database, custom recipes, keeps you mindful of intake
apps.weak: Nearly empty barcode scanner, small brand database means manual entry, crashes when entering weight, lost login and history, no Apple Health sync
apps.whoFor: People who want a no-frills manual tracker of food, weight and calories and will build their own food list

apps.title: Weight Tracker — Scelta
apps.verdict: A weight tracker built around trend and light gamification with coins and BMI. Daily weigh-ins and a months-long graph genuinely keep many people on track for years. But Apple Watch sync is shaky: entries on the watch and phone live separately, logging weight on the watch is fiddly, and the math around percentages and goals confuses a lot of users.
apps.loved: The multi-year trend graph, the BMI metric and moderate coin gamification, plus a responsive developer who ships fixes fast.
apps.weak: Watch and phone do not sync with each other, the percentage and goal math is odd, you cannot fix a wrong entry or add historical data, and there is no landscape mode on iPad.
apps.whoFor: People who weigh in every day and watch the long-term trend rather than a single number.

quotes.text: Weighing daily and paying attention to trend has helped me stay on track with my eating and walking goals for three years now! Thank you!

apps.title: Weight Monitor, BMI Calculator
apps.verdict: A tidy weight tracker with BMI, a trend graph, progress photos and widgets. Logging weight is simple, and months of history and body shots are clearly visible, with a one-time purchase instead of a subscription. It is spoiled by pushy achievements after every weigh-in and notifications that shame you for skipping, plus shaky Apple Health import after changing phones.
apps.loved: A clean simple interface, the trend graph and multi-angle progress photos, home-screen widgets, a one-time purchase and real stories of dropping a hundred pounds or more.
apps.weak: Achievements and backup prompts pop up after every weigh-in, notifications shame you for skipping, the plan caps you at two units a week, the promised free turns into a charge, and Health import sometimes breaks.
apps.whoFor: People who want a visual tracker with progress photos and a one-time payment and are ready to switch off the nagging notifications.

quotes.text: i notice that the target weight on the checkpoint keeps changing. whenever i enter a new weight if it is close to the checkpoint it changes. i do find it confusing and a little annoying that it keeps changing

I don’t like that they take the Duolingo route of passive aggressive notifications if you aren't actively using the app. If I needed passive aggressive nagging about my weight I would have a relationship with my mother.
I’ve been searching for an app that does comparison/progress photos of at least 3 angles finally found this app.

apps.title: Progress Body Tracker: My BMI
apps.verdict: A body tracker built around before-and-after photos and measurements, with weight and BMI as a side note. After a big redesign people lost their measurement history and their paid Pro turned back into a subscription. Sync has been broken for many for years, and the photo compare zooms shots inconsistently, so honest side-by-sides are hard.
apps.loved: Before-and-after photos in one place genuinely motivate, you see progress with your own eyes. It used to offer up to fifteen measurement fields and a handy CSV export.
apps.weak: The redesign wiped years of measurements and stripped paid Pro back to a subscription. Sync fails, the number of measurements was cut, and photo compare distorts scale.
apps.whoFor: People who track by photos and measurements rather than weight alone, and who are willing to back up regularly so they do not lose history.

quotes.text: this app makes it easy for me to keep track of my progress all in one place :) And it helps keep my motivated to see the side my side comparisons of my fat loss journey
the photo progress feature zooms in on some pictures and out on others making it hard to actually compare. Hope they fix it, or at least give me control to resize within the app

I have been using this app for years to keep track of health and measurement data. This morning when I logged in after the latest upgrade it was ALL gone. There was no warning to back up data, no hint that this was going to happen with the new version.

apps.title: Weight Loss Bet by HealthyWage
apps.loved: Money on the line as strong motivation, real large payouts, step and weight-loss challenges, built lasting habits, keeps you accountable
apps.weak: Buggy verified weigh-ins and video uploads, confusing and poor bet odds, pushes unhealthy weight-loss targets, hard to cancel with slow support, clunky navigation
apps.whoFor: People who lose weight best under a money-on-the-line bet and can handle a rough, buggy app

apps.title: Formula － weight loss diet app
apps.loved: Meal ideas and recipes, barcode scanning, planning calories days ahead, reminders to think about food, real weight loss on the Mediterranean plan
apps.weak: Misleading ads about what the app is, charges after cancellation, extra upsell for promised features, clunky food search, thin food database
apps.whoFor: People drawn to a Mediterranean-diet food diary who read the billing terms carefully first

apps.title: Value Diary - Weight Loss Diet
apps.verdict: A food and weight tracker built on the old Weight Watchers points, cheaper than the original for a yearly fee. You keep a food diary, scan barcodes and watch your weight trend. But after the subscription auto-renews some people lose access to what they paid for, restore purchase fails, and the scanner and points math sometimes return wild numbers.
apps.loved: It brings back the old colored WW plans cheaper than the original, with a large food database and a points calculator. The weight trend and food diary are handy, and support helps when reached.
apps.weak: After the yearly auto-renewal access to paid features vanishes, and restore purchase does not work. The barcode scanner is weak, points are sometimes absurd, and support is unreachable without logging in.
apps.whoFor: Fans of the old Weight Watchers points who will tolerate subscription hassle for a cheap alternative.

apps.title: TadaPal: Weight Loss Friend
apps.verdict: More of a gamified weight-loss friend with an AI food scanner than a pure weight tracker. The Tada character motivates and praises healthy eating, and some report serious weight loss. But the calorie scanner is noticeably off in both directions, the food database has gaps, and the once-free macros now sit behind a subscription.
apps.loved: The cute companion character that praises healthy meals and keeps you going, a working AI food scanner, and real weight loss for some users.
apps.weak: The AI scanner over- and under-estimates calories, the food database is incomplete and you cannot add your own item, macros were pulled from the free version, plus glitches and silent support.
apps.whoFor: People who value friendly motivation and food logging over precise weight tracking and are willing to double-check calories by hand.

apps.title: Omo: Healthy Weight Loss App
apps.loved: Scanning barcodes and plates, easy food logging, water and fasting tracking, visible weight-loss results, responsive support
apps.weak: Quiz dead-ends on a paywall, exercise tracking costs extra, wrong calorie counts from scans, glitchy food search, charges after cancelling
apps.whoFor: People who mainly want guided food logging and weight loss and are fine paying a subscription

apps.title: BetterTogether: Weight Loss
apps.verdict: A group weight-loss tracker with teams, challenges and chat. Weight is entered by hand, and auto-sync with Apple Health and smart scales barely works even though the data is already there. The weigh-in button sometimes disappears, the app crashes with a login error, and Pro popups appear before you can even look around.
apps.loved: Teams and shared challenges keep motivation up, it is nice to lose weight with family or coworkers. Food entry is simple, and the leaderboards and chat in a safe circle land well.
apps.weak: No proper auto-sync with Apple Health and scales, so weight must be typed manually. Pro popups and hidden charges at signup, and the weigh-in button and login sometimes break.
apps.whoFor: Small groups of friends or family who value mutual support and the thrill of competition more than automation accuracy.

quotes.text: It's frustrating to manually input my weight when my smart scale already syncs that data seamlessly with Apple Health.

apps.title: BMI Calculator‰
apps.loved: Fast and simple to use, clean BMI result with decimals, handy for quick checks, worked ad-free for years
apps.weak: Aggressive pop-up ads during input, fake storage-full and scam pop-ups, no fractional height entry, no Apple Health sync, ignores muscle and sex
apps.whoFor: People who want a fast BMI check and can tolerate the new ads, or would pay to remove them

apps.title: My Diet Coach - Weight Loss
apps.loved: Fun and motivating old avatar version, simple food and weight logging, cute goal options, large food database, more interactive than most
apps.weak: Beloved avatar version removed, once-free features moved behind a paywall, no login so data and profile lost, data wiped after updates, broken barcode scanner
apps.whoFor: People who want a light, playful food diary and can live without account backup or the old avatar

apps.title: Weight Loss Simple Tracker App
apps.verdict: A simple weight and BMI tracker with an avatar that gets heavier and slimmer along with you. For some it is a thrill, but many feel shamed, the avatar draws extra weight and offends, and inclusivity of skin tone and body is thin. Basics like BMI, changing the avatar and total pounds lost are locked behind a subscription of around 30 dollars a year, and there are intrusive ads.
apps.loved: The avatar that slims down with you genuinely motivates, seeing the graph line crawl downward. Simple and visual, tracks weight and body-fat percentage.
apps.weak: The avatar shames and draws extra weight, inclusivity is thin, and it hurts some people. BMI, avatar changes and total lost sit behind a subscription, and ads are intrusive.
apps.whoFor: People motivated by a visual avatar and graph, with solid self-esteem, who are willing to pay extra for basic features.

quotes.text: as you enter your weight it shows a picture or an icon of how big they think you are and that’s not right. It makes me feel discouraged as I get heavier and not healthier.

apps.title: Weight loss tracker - BMI
apps.verdict: A free weight and BMI tracker with notes, photos and a passcode. Entry is simple, but two limits have annoyed the whole thread for years, the graph shows only 7 or 30 days and never lets you see the full journey. Data sometimes vanishes entirely, does not transfer to a new phone, and there are heavy ads with no way to pay them away.
apps.loved: Simple and free, you enter weight and add notes, photos and a passcode. The monthly graph motivates, you see the weight going down.
apps.weak: The graph is locked to 7 or 30 days, and you cannot see the full journey despite years of requests. Data suddenly wipes, does not transfer to a new phone, and ads are heavy with no removal option.
apps.whoFor: People happy with a free simple tracker over short stretches, who back up their data and tolerate ads.

quotes.text: Doesn’t show cumulative weight loss or progress beyond 30 days so not sure what the point of this app is
I love this app and use it for my weight loss journey. you can change the chart data range. It’s made tracking much easier and increased my motivation when I see my weight go down
I opened my app today to discover 2 YEARS of daily information gone, all of it (and no i absolutely did not manually reset all data).

apps.title: Kompanion: Weight Loss Plan
apps.loved: Helpful intermittent-fasting timer and stages, real weight loss, interactive insights, recipes, keeps you honest about food
apps.weak: Charges without consent and refused refunds, free version logs only one food a day, inaccurate freezing food scanner, no dark mode or widgets, heavy paywall
apps.whoFor: People focused on intermittent fasting who watch billing closely and will pay for the full app

apps.title: BMI Calculator for Weight Loss
apps.verdict: A simple BMI and ideal-weight calculator. After updates some people got stuck on kilograms with no pounds and inches option, and weight entry sometimes breaks. Worse, BMI categories are computed wrong, a healthy range is flagged as overweight, there is no age input, and ads push aggressively.
apps.loved: A clean and fast calculator with no popups for some people, handy for figuring BMI and ideal weight. It helps some folks at work every day.
apps.weak: BMI categories are computed wrong, a healthy weight is flagged as overweight and called fat. After updates it got stuck on kilograms, entry breaks, ads are aggressive, and age is ignored.
apps.whoFor: People who need a quick one-off BMI figure and will double-check the category themselves rather than take the label to heart.

apps.title: BMI Calculator – Weight Loss
apps.loved: Instant BMI result, very easy to use, clean quick input, handy as a rough check
apps.weak: Wrong healthy ranges label teens obese, dangerously low BMI shown as normal, ignores muscle mass, triggers body-image and ED harm, no sync between devices
apps.whoFor: Adults who want a quick rough BMI check and know its limits, not teens or anyone recovering from an eating disorder

apps.title: Glowise: GLP-1 Tracker & Diary
apps.verdict: A GLP-1 diary for shots, symptoms, water, protein and weight trend in one place. The idea is good, but you cannot try it, payment is demanded before you can do anything. The food database is weak, portion recognition misses, you can log only one symptom after a shot, and the max weight caps at 330 pounds, which hurts people starting heavier.
apps.loved: Everything for GLP-1 in one place, shots, protein, water, side effects and weight trend, no jumping between apps. Those it fits praise the ease and clarity.
apps.weak: Nothing works without a subscription, payment before any action and no trial. Weak food database, one symptom per shot, weight capped at 330 pounds, portion recognition off.
apps.whoFor: People on GLP-1 who need a single diary for shots and side effects and are willing to pay upfront blind, if their starting weight is under 330 pounds.

quotes.text: It mentions tracking your symptoms after shots but will not allow you to choose more than 1.

apps.title: Jurney: AI Weight Loss Coach
apps.verdict: It is essentially an AI weight-loss coach, but you can barely try it: onboarding asks questions for about ten minutes, then demands a subscription, and there is no way past it without paying. Weight logging, trends and Health or scale sync are impossible to judge, real users never reach those screens. Those who paid report losing weight, but they are a minority.
apps.loved: People who broke through the paywall mention real weight loss and motivation, some report eight pounds down in three weeks.
apps.weak: The paywall blocks the whole entrance, subscription ads pop over the screen every few seconds, and the pay button sometimes crashes with an error. Teens without a card simply cannot use it.
apps.whoFor: People ready to pay for an AI coach right away who do not plan to test it for free.

apps.title: BMI Calculator ~
apps.verdict: A calculator that looks cute but is wrong about the one thing that matters. Users catch it on incorrect BMI, height cannot be set above five foot nine and has no decimals, so the number matches almost no one. Trends and sync are secondary when the basic math is off, and it even asks for money for it.
apps.loved: A pleasant look and a positive, supportive tone, simple input, and some teens like the gentle framing that does not pressure the number.
apps.weak: BMI is calculated incorrectly, height is capped and has no decimals, the basic calculator asks for money, and the app congratulates you on gaining a hundred pounds and mislabels a slim person as overweight.
apps.whoFor: At most people who want a rough weight reference and do not care about accurate BMI.
